blocks.text: **The task.** Group the elements of a matrix by diagonal. Each diagonal runs from bottom-left to top-right.
The whole problem collapses once you notice this: **every cell on the same diagonal has the same value of `r + c`**.
Cells with sum 0 form the first diagonal, sum 1 the second, and so on. A matrix of R rows and C columns has `R + C - 1` diagonals.
No clever traversal order needed. Sweep the grid normally and file each cell into a bucket keyed by `r + c`:

The plain row-major sweep visits `(0,2)` before `(1,1)` before `(2,0)`, so each bucket fills top-right to bottom-left. If you need the opposite, either iterate rows downward or reverse each bucket afterwards.
The zigzag variant — alternating direction per diagonal — is just this with `if (d % 2 === 0) diagonals[d].reverse()`.
Diagonals running top-left to bottom-right share a constant `r - c` instead. That value can be negative, so offset by `cols - 1` to index an array:
**Time: O(R x C)** — one ordinary sweep. **Space: O(R x C)** for the output.
Worth remembering as a category of trick: find the quantity that stays constant across the group you care about, and use it as a key.
